summary.decisions: One stable key 'petal_panic_store' holding {progress, settings, saveMeta}; in-memory cache as source of truth with every mutation persisting the whole document atomically; normalize() tolerates missing/mistyped fields on load; storage injected lazily via globalThis.localStorage with setStorage hook for tests (mirrors input.js createInput pattern).
summary.tradeoffs: updateProgress mutator receives the full store document (store.progress.completedAreas etc.) rather than the progress section directly — matches plan snippet style where saveMeta is set as store.saveMeta; callers must use store.progress.* for progress fields.
summary.done: Added petal-panic/js/systems/progressStore.js: single localStorage JSON document (key 'petal_panic_store') with progress/settings/saveMeta sections, safe defaults (DEFAULT_PROGRESS v1, DEFAULT_SETTINGS), and APIs loadStore/saveStore/updateProgress/updateSettings/markMediaUnlocked/hasSave/clearRunSave/resetStore plus setStorage/_resetCache test hooks. Added node:test suite js/test/progressStore.test.js (10 tests) covering empty/invalid storage, atomic mutate+persist, reload survival, hasSave semantics, storage-denied fallback.
summary.lessons_learned: Plan snippet's updateProgress example writes store.completedAreas directly but also store.saveMeta at top level — resolved by making the mutator receive the full document so both styles work consistently (saveMeta top-level, progress nested under store.progress).

summary.tradeoffs: None — state machine only, no screen wiring yet (later tasks). progressStore not needed at this layer since routing is pure state.
summary.done: Added MENU(10), OPTIONS(11), LEVEL_SELECT(12), BOSS_RUSH(13), MEDIA(14) states to petal-panic/js/core/state.js (S + STATE_NAMES) and extended TRANSITIONS: HOME→MENU; MENU→SELECT/PLAY/LEVEL_SELECT/BOSS_RUSH/MEDIA/REMAP/OPTIONS; PAUSE gains MENU+OPTIONS; OPTIONS→MENU|PAUSE; LEVEL_SELECT/BOSS_RUSH→MENU|PLAY|AREA_ENTRY; MEDIA→MENU; REMAP also returns to MENU. Added node:test suite petal-panic/js/test/stateMenu.test.js covering all acceptance criteria plus negative cases.
summary.decisions: Kept the single centralized TRANSITIONS map rather than per-state handlers; added S.MENU to REMAP's return set so Controls opened from the hub can go back there; OPTIONS returns to both MENU and PAUSE to serve as the shared options screen.
summary.lessons_learned: state.js is importable headless with plain node ESM — no DOM stubs needed for transition tests.

summary.done: Added canvas-drawn Menu hub screen to petal-panic/js/ui/screens.js: eight options (New Game, Continue/No Save, Level Select, Boss Rush, Media, Controls, Options, Credits) with the pause-style centered list, pink focus pill, and keycap nav bar; Continue label/enabled driven live by progressStore.hasSave(); up/down wrap and skip disabled entries; confirm routes New Game→SELECT, Continue→AREA_ENTRY (§2.3 owns resume), Level Select/Boss Rush/Media/OPTIONS/Controls→REMAP per the 2.1 transition map; back returns HOME. Wired MENU into drawScreen + screenOnAction dispatch, screenReset (Menu.reset), and render.js full-screen skip list. Fixed deferred 2.1 item: remapParent now resolves from {HOME, PAUSE, MENU} so REMAP opened from MENU returns to MENU. Added node:test suite js/test/menuScreen.test.js (9 tests).
summary.decisions: Reused Pause's exact ergonomics pattern (roundRect focus pill, ▸ prefix, drawNavBar/navHintEntries select_layout chips) rather than a new style; Menu.options() is a single source of truth shared by draw/onAction/focus-skip so enabled state can never diverge; wrote test saves via loadStore().saveMeta + saveStore (documented API) because updateProgress mutates only the progress section and cannot set top-level saveMeta.
summary.lessons_learned: updateProgress's mutator receives store.progress, not the full document — setting store.saveMeta inside it silently lands under progress.saveMeta and hasSave() stays false (the store's own test suite uses loadStore().saveMeta = ... for this reason). Also note run-all baseline on clean tree: 5 pre-existing failures (bombGameplay/dustCloud/shockwave + pickerRide/takeoffPicker) identical before and after this change.
summary.tradeoffs: Continue confirms to AREA_ENTRY without saveMeta restore logic — that flow is owned by task 2.3; the transition edge already exists from 2.1. Credits confirm is a no-op until its presentation lands in a later task.

summary.lessons_learned: headless-smoke.mjs fails on a clean tree too (composeArea: no compatible macros — macro loading in node env), pre-existing and unrelated. progressStore.saveMeta must be written at document top level, never inside updateProgress.
summary.done: Added three lifecycle ops in petal-panic/js/systems/lifecycle.js: newGameFromMenu() (clearRunSave + SELECT), continueFromMenu(hero) (restore currentLevel/currentArea from loadStore().saveMeta, open AREA_ENTRY via showAreaEntry), saveCurrentRun(hero) (writes top-level saveMeta {level, area, score via calculateScore(traceStats.total), timestamp} through loadStore/saveStore). Wired Menu hub in screens.js: New Game action now calls newGameFromMenu(); Continue option switched from go:S.AREA_ENTRY to action:'continue' calling continueFromMenu(_menuHero); added setMenuHero/getMenuHero registration. update.js registers the live hero via setHeroRef (boot + every hero swap). New test file js/test/menuRunFlow.test.js (8 tests) covers all four acceptance bullets incl. storage round-trip.
summary.decisions: Continue routing moved from option-level 'go' data to an action handler so the saveMeta restore happens before the transition; hero passed via setMenuHero registration (update.js owns the live hero ref) rather than window globals. Save & Quit write side exposed as saveCurrentRun() for task 4.2 to call; the PAUSE→MENU transition stays with 4.2.
summary.tradeoffs: continueFromMenu tolerates a null hero (bare-test path) by presenting the entry screen with the saved level/area and starting lives; real gameplay always has the registered live hero. saveCurrentRun sets store.saveMeta directly on the loaded document + saveStore (not updateProgress) since saveMeta is top-level per task 1.1.

summary.done: Added petal-panic/js/ui/levelSelectModel.js (pure model over LEVEL_CONFIGS + progress): buildLevelMap(progress) → exactly 8 markers {level,name,status,selected} with no zone nodes; buildSubAreasForLevel(level,progress) → exactly 5 choices X-1..X-4/X-B with {level,zone,label,boss,status,tooltip,start:{level,area}}. Level status: completed when all 5 areas done, available when the immediately preceding level is fully completed (level 1 always), else locked. Sub-area unlock chain: prev sub-area completed (level 1 area 1 default-unlocked; other levels' first area gates on prev level's X-B); locked entries carry tooltip 'Pass <prev> to unlock'. Added js/test/levelSelectModel.test.js (13 tests). Plan verify command passes (buildLevelMap length 8).
summary.decisions: Model is pure: screen passes in the progress section; no localStorage/state imports so it stays node-testable headlessly. Area ids reuse formatAreaId's convention ('X-N', 'X-B') matching what lifecycle writes to completedAreas. AREA_BOSS=5 exported for screens/tests. Mistyped/null progress degrades to defaults (mirrors progressStore.normalize rules) rather than throwing.
summary.failures: None — 13/13 new tests pass; plan verify command prints 8. Full suite 86/93 with my file included; the 7 failures (bombGameplay, dustCloud, input, lifecycle, pickerRide, shockwave, takeoffPicker) are pre-existing and reproduce identically with my changes stashed (85/92 baseline).
summary.tradeoffs: Chose strict sequential gating for level availability (a later level unlocks only when its immediate predecessor is fully completed incl. boss), matching the milestone's 'what must be passed before unlocking' framing; a permissive any-predecessor rule would have contradicted that.
summary.lessons_learned: First draft used 'any earlier level complete' for availability — wrong; availability must chain through the IMMEDIATE predecessor or every level unlocks at once. Verified pre-existing suite failures via git stash before attributing them.

The shared roundRect() helper draws via arcTo corners, not a native roundRect call — headless geometry assertions must key off arcTo corner coordinates (x+w, y) rather than method names. Proxy-based ctx stubs record property sets (globalAlpha etc.) separately from method calls.
summary.tradeoffs: Level names come from levelSelectModel (LEVEL_CONFIGS) while area-entry uses world/level.js LEVELS — only level 1 exists in LEVELS today, so starting levels 2+ shows 'Level N' fallback until multi-level world support lands (pre-existing gap, not introduced here). Confirm routes through startArea which resets specials and records an entry snapshot — same semantics as a normal mid-run area advance.
summary.done: Added LevelSelect screen in screens.js (two-pane: 8 level markers row + 5 sub-area chips for selected level on the left, right-side detail card with lock hint/play hint), wired into drawScreen/screenOnAction/screenReset and render.js full-screen skip list; generalized update.js AREA_ENTRY install hook from MENU to also cover LEVEL_SELECT; confirm starts the focused unlocked zone via lifecycle.startArea → showAreaEntry. New headless test js/test/levelSelectScreen.test.js (9 tests) covers all acceptance bullets.
summary.decisions: Focus model is {levelIdx, zoneIdx} into the pure model arrays; navigation skips locked levels/zones (wrap-around) so focus can only rest on playable content; locked-focus confirm is a no-op safety net. Zone/checkpoint installation reuses the existing MENU→AREA_ENTRY hook by generalizing its from-state check rather than duplicating it. Detail-card tooltip text comes straight from the model's tooltip field ('Pass X-Y to unlock').

summary.tradeoffs: Music/SFX toggles persist but consume nothing yet (no audio engine by design); acceptance says 'three toggle rows' but DEFAULT_SETTINGS has four keys — implemented all four per the snippet.
summary.lessons_learned: drawPrompt prefixes row labels with '▸ '/two-spaces, so recording-ctx text assertions must strip that prefix before matching; effects module exposes Effects.update(dt) for advancing instance lifetimes in tests.
summary.done: Added Options screen (js/ui/screens.js): four toggle rows (Music/SFX/Screen Shake/Vibration) rendered via the shared drawOptionList pause-style renderer with ON/OFF state on the label; up/down focus (wrap), left/right/confirm toggles persisting immediately through progressStore.updateSettings; origin tracking (optionsOrigin, mirroring remapParent) so back returns MENU or PAUSE; wired into drawScreen, screenOnAction, and screenReset(to, from). Settings consumers wired where they exist: Effects.triggerShake() now suppresses camera shake when settings.screenShake is false (single funnel — render only reads getShakeOffset); touchControls buzz() skips navigator.vibrate when settings.vibration is false. Music/SFX are honest no-ops (no audio system exists; tuning.js marks audio deferred) — values persist for a future audio engine. New test file js/test/optionsScreen.test.js (9 tests, headless DOM-stub pattern incl. persistence round-trip via _resetCache).
summary.decisions: screenShake gate placed at Effects.triggerShake (the single kick funnel) rather than in render.js's getShakeOffset read, so declarative carrier-fired shakes are also suppressed consistently; vibration gate at buzz() (sole haptics funnel); optionsOrigin defaults to MENU and is captured in screenReset exactly like remapParent.

4.2.name: Pause menu Save and Quit integration

summary.tradeoffs: Dropped the old 'Quit to Home' option per plan spec (the five-option list replaces it); back/Esc still resumes so no quit path is lost.
summary.done: Pause screen now has five data-driven options (Resume, Retry Level, Save & Quit, Controls, Options) using Menu's {go/action} pattern; Save & Quit calls saveCurrentRun(hero) then transitions PAUSE→MENU; Controls→REMAP and Options→OPTIONS capture origin PAUSE via existing screenReset logic; hero wired through screenOnAction with getMenuHero() fallback. Added js/test/pauseSaveQuit.test.js (8 tests, all pass).
summary.lessons_learned: screens.js does not re-export Remap — tests must import core/remap.js directly. The old 4th pause option was 'Quit to Home' (not 'Quit'); its actions.quit handler was preserved as a semantic-action path even though no menu row routes to it anymore.
summary.failures: None — pre-existing bck/screens82.test.js fails identically before this change (broken relative import paths in that legacy file, not caused by 4.2).
summary.decisions: Used Menu's F5 data-driven routing shape ({label, enabled, go|action}) for Pause.options() instead of hardcoded switch-on-index; kept onAction(action, actions, hero) signature matching GameOver's convention, with saveCurrentRun falling back to the registered menu hero when no hero is passed.
